title: Retail loan book: 6-month delinquency review

findings.headline: Delinquency has risen for three quarters running
findings.detail: The 30-days-past-due rate at 6 months (dpd30) is 8.8% overall (440 of 5,000 loans). It rose from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, up 6.2 points. Q1 26 loans may not yet have six months of history, so check how the outcome is measured.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high default and missed first payments
findings.detail: Nine phone values repeat across 42 loans. In that group, 83.3% reached 30 days past due, against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment, against 2.3% overall. This is a possible fraud signal.

findings.headline: Personal and Card loans are driving the deterioration
findings.detail: Personal loan delinquency rose from 9.3% in Q1 25 to 21.0% in Q1 26. Card rose from 11.2% to 20.2%. Car stayed near 6% and Home near 0.5%, so the problem is concentrated in unsecured-style products.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed borrowers show higher delinquency
findings.detail: Digital loans are at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch. Self-employed borrowers are at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried. Digital also has a lower average bureau score, 715.4 against 733.7 for Branch.

findings.headline: Income is missing mainly for Partner-channel loans
findings.detail: Income is missing on 6.9% of rows. Of those, 90.8% are Partner loans, and 39.7% of Partner loans have no income. Any affordability analysis would be skewed for that channel.

next_steps: Review the 42 loans sharing phone numbers for application fraud, and check whether the Partner or Digital channels originated them.
Break Personal and Card delinquency in Q4 25 and Q1 26 down by channel and employment, and confirm the six-month outcome is mature for Q1 26.
Ask the Partner channel why income is missing on 39.7% of loans, and decide whether to tighten data capture at origination.

reviews.note: Quarterly rates 6.6, 7.8, 9.7, 12.8 rise three times running; 12.8 minus 6.6 is 6.2 points. Maturity caveat is fair.

findings.detail: Nine phone values repeat across 42 loans. In that group 83.3% reached 30 days past due (about 35 loans) against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment against 2.3% overall. The group is under 1% of the book, and the summary does not show why it behaves this way, so it needs checking.

findings.headline: Rising delinquency is concentrated in Personal and Card loans
findings.detail: Personal loan delinquency went from 9.3% in Q1 25 to 21.0% in Q1 26. Card went from 11.2% to 20.2%. Car stayed between 4.7% and 6.3%, and Home stayed at or below 1.1%.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed loans show higher delinquency
findings.detail: Digital loans are at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and Partner is at 7.2%. Self-employed borrowers are at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried. Bureau score does not explain this: salaried and self-employed averages are almost the same (723.6 and 723.1).

findings.headline: Income is missing mainly for Partner-channel loans
findings.detail: Income is missing on 6.9% of rows. Of those, 90.8% are Partner loans, and 39.7% of Partner loans have no income. Any income-based analysis would be weaker for that channel.

next_steps: Review the 42 loans that share phone numbers, and check which channels and products they came from before drawing any conclusion.
Split Personal and Card delinquency for Q4 25 and Q1 26 by channel and employment, and confirm the six-month outcome is complete for Q1 26 loans.
Ask the Partner channel why income is missing on 39.7% of its loans, and decide whether data capture at origination needs tightening.
conclusion: Delinquency is worsening, from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, and the rise sits in Personal and Card loans, while Car and Home are steady. First, confirm that the six-month outcome is complete for recent loans, then split the Personal and Card rise by channel and employment to see where to act.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show causes, confirm fraud, or check how the six-month outcome was measured.
